children: Palm oil futures closed higher, snapping a multiday losing streak. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for December delivery rose 3 ringgit to 4,771 ringgit a ton. Despite the rebound, prices are likely to be under pressure due to expectations of higher inventories, according to David Ng, a trader at Kuala Lumpur-based Iceberg X. He expects palm oil prices to be supported at around 4,700 ringgit to 4,750 ringgit a ton, and sees them facing resistance near 4,850 ringgit-4,900 ringgit a ton. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
